title: Smashing Magazine, “The Split Personality of Brutalist Web Development”
lede: An essay that splits web brutalism into l’Internet brut, built from raw HTML, and l’Internet fou, built for shock.
summary: Frederick O’Brien’s 2020 essay: raw HTML brutalism (light ground, black text, blue links) versus audacious brutalism.

evidence.note: Article text read on 2026-10-02. The publication time (8 January 2020) is in the page’s metadata, and the author link is on the page. The article’s screenshots were not inspected.

styles.note: Names and describes the raw core of the style and separates it from the audacious branch.

context: “Type One: l’Internet Brut … where the raw materials are HTML and, to a lesser extent, CSS. The backgrounds are light, the text is black, and the hyperlinks are blue.”

Examples it names for the raw type: the first website, David Bryant Copeland’s [Brutalist Web Design](ref:copeland-brutalist-web-design-guidelines), Craigslist, Wikipedia, the old A List Apart, old Reddit, Bloomberg, and Freecycle.
“Type Two: l’Internet Fou” covers the many “brutalist” sites built to provoke. It quotes Vitaly Friedman: brutalism in architecture is “unconcerned aesthetics, not intentionally broken aesthetics”.
interpretation: Its Type One is the scope of [Brutalist web design](style:brutalist-web-design). Some of its examples, such as Bloomberg, are bolder than default HTML and need a capture before they count as evidence.
borrow: Treat HTML as the material: let the structure of the document set the look, and shape each page around its content.
